title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
content:
This study introduces a green, aqueous binder combining helical proteins, polyvinyl alcohol, and glycerol for lithium‐sulfur batteries. The protein's “molecular spring” structure effectively buffers volume expansion, while its polar groups strongly anchor polysulfides to suppress the shuttle effect and boost redox kinetics. This synergistic design ultimately enables exceptional long‐term cycling stability.








ABSTRACT
Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g−1 and retains 487.9 mAh g−1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li2Ta2OCl10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm−1)
content:
This work presents a new crystalline oxyhalide, Li2Ta2OCl10, built from [Ta2OCl10]2− dimers. The disorder induced by ball‐milling drives the dramatic 5000‐fold increase in ionic conductivity to reach 11 mS.cm−1. The material shows promise as a solid electrolyte for batteries and opens new prospects for the discovery of new dimer‐based compounds.








ABSTRACT
All‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy‐density limits of conventional lithium‐ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo‐mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast‐ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li2Ta2OCl10, synthesized via a simple low‐temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta2OCl10]2− dimers and exhibits a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm−1. Ball milling dramatically enhances Li+ transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm−1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid‐like Li+ sublattice. Li2Ta2OCl10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89–3.70 V vs. LixIn and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li2Ta2OCl10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li–M–O–Cl family as a fertile design space for next‐generation solid electrolytes.

title: Trash to Treasure: PFAS‐Functionalized MOFs for Boosted Piezocatalytic H2 Production
content:
A novel pollutant‐as‐functional‐additive strategy is developed via postsynthetic modification of MOF‐808(Hf) with perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), a typical PFAS pollutant. The modification boosts the dipole moment of the MOFs, enhances their piezoelectricity to promote efficient electron‐hole separation, thus delivering ultrahigh piezocatalytic hydrogen evolution activity, with broad universality for Hf‐based MOFs bearing unsaturated metal sites.








ABSTRACT
Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) hold broad prospects in piezocatalysis because of their high surface area, porosity, and tunable structures, yet pristine MOFs frequently suffer from poor piezocatalytic response. Herein, this study pioneers a novel strategy using pollutant perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) as a functional additive to post‐synthetically modify MOF‐808(Hf), fabricating MOF‐808(Hf)‐F for piezocatalytic hydrogen production. PFHxA modification remarkably enhances the polarity of MOF‐808(Hf) (dipole moment from 8.90 to 12.58 D) and piezoelectricity (d33 from 63.70 to 234.30 pm V−1), boosting electron‐hole separation verified by electrochemical and in situ photoluminescence characterizations. Consequently, MOF‐808(Hf)‐F achieves an excellent piezocatalytic H2 evolution rate of 2811.4 µmol g−1 h−1, 10.5‐fold higher than the pristine counterpart and superior to that of numerous reported MOF‐based piezocatalysts. In addition, MOF‐808(Hf) achieves a PFHxA removal efficiency of approximately 40.1% from water. This work realizes simultaneous per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal and efficient energy production, with excellent universality for Hf‐based MOFs with unsaturated metal sites.

title: 16.52% Efficiency All‐Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells via Al‐Doped ZnO/SnO2 Electron Transport Bilayer for Improved Interfacial Energy‐Level Alignment
content:
This work reports a new approach in enhancing efficiency of CsPbI2Br perovskite solar cells by introducing Al‐doped ZnO/SnO2 electron transport bilayer for improved interfacial energy‐level alignment without doping or passivation of the perovskite, without resorting passivation or doping the perovskites, leading to a champion power conversion efficiency of 16.52% along with a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.33 V.








ABSTRACT
Interfacial energy‐level misalignment in all‐inorganic perovskite solar cells generally causes inefficient charge extraction. Here, we propose an Al‐doped ZnO (AZO)/SnO2 electron transport bilayer to improve energy‐level alignment in CsPbI2Br‐based PSCs. By this approach, we achieved a champion efficiency of 16.52%, which is the highest reported value for all‐inorganic CsPbI2Br PSCs without doping or passivation of the perovskite, along with a high VOC of 1.33 V. AZO‐based devices substantially outperform ZnO‐based controls, delivering a PCE of 16.52% versus 15.21%, with suppressed dark current, reduced trap density, lower non‐radiative recombination, and smaller hysteresis. The AZO device retains 80% of its initial efficiency after 662 h of continuous illumination, compared with only 312 h for the ZnO counterpart. Al3+ substitution for Zn2+ elevates the ZnO conduction band minimum, establishing a favorable cascade alignment among SnO2/AZO/perovskite that lowers the electron extraction barrier and blocks hole backflow. Al doping also suppresses oxygen vacancies, reducing interfacial trap‐state density and enhancing perovskite crystallinity. Efficient charge extraction further suppresses Ag electrode degradation and corrosion, contributing to long‐term stability. This work establishes a rational interfacial engineering approach using an AZO/SnO2 bilayer for efficient and stable all‐inorganic perovskite solar cells.

title: Scanless Centimeter‐Scale Microstereolithography Enabled by Source‐Plane Angular Conditioning
content:
A source‐plane angular‐conditioning (SPAC) architecture enables efficient coupling of a large‐area LCD to finite‐aperture projection optics, overcoming the conventional resolution–area trade‐off in projection microstereolithography. The proposed LµSL platform achieves micron‐scale projected pixels and centimeter‐scale fabrication in a single exposure without stitching or mechanical scanning.








ABSTRACT
Achieving centimeter‐scale scanless microstereolithography remains challenging in conventional projection microstereolithography (PµSL), where improving resolution inevitably restricts printable area due to the finite number of pixels. High‐pixel‐density LCD modulators provide a promising pathway to relax this limitation, but their large emission area introduces severe optical coupling and illumination nonuniformity in reduction projection systems. Here, we introduce source‐plane angular conditioning implemented in an LCD‐based microstereolithography (LµSL) platform. This optical strategy reshapes the emission angular distribution of a planar light source, enabling efficient pupil matching and uniform wide‐field illumination for scanless projection across centimeter‐scale areas. Using an 8K LCD modulator and wide‐angle lenses with different focal lengths, the system achieves projected pixel pitches of ≈1–3 µm over printable areas of ≈0.8–2.4 cm in a single exposure without mechanical scanning, stitching, or relay optics. Diverse microstructures—including stripe arrays, microneedle arrays, octet‐truss lattices, and complex freeform geometries—are fabricated to demonstrate the platform's capability for heterogeneous, multi‐scale microfabrication. The proposed optical framework establishes a practical route toward high‐resolution, large‐area microfabrication and provides a scalable platform for applications in microfluidics, biomedical devices, photonics, and architected materials.

title: Polarity‐Mediated β‐Phase Reconstruction and Dual‐Salt Synergy for Fast Li+ Transport in Solid‐State Li Metal Batteries
content:
Molecular‐polarity synergy combining TCNE‐driven β‐phase reconstruction and dualsalt engineering optimizes ion transport and interphase, enabling high‐performance PVDF solid polymer electrolytes for long‐life lithium‐metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) hold great promise for safe Li metal batteries but are hindered by low ionic conductivity and insufficient salt dissociation. Here, we propose a molecular polarity‐mediated synergistic strategy that integrates tetracyanoethylene (TCNE)‐induced β‐phase reconstruction with dual‐salt chemistry to simultaneously optimize ion transport kinetics and interfacial stability. In this strategy, the strongly electron‐withdrawing cyano groups of TCNE engage in dipole interactions with PVDF chains, triggering a nonpolar α‐to‐polar β‐phase transition, which facilitates salt dissociation and shortens the Li+ migration pathway; the dual‐salt system further ensures fast Li+ conduction while constructing a robust, LiF/boron‐rich interphase via LiDFOB. The resulting TCNE‐modified PVDF electrolyte (PTDL) delivers a high ionic conductivity of 9.32 × 10−4 S cm−1, a high Li+ transference number of 0.76, and a wide electrochemical window of 4.8 V. Thus, the symmetric cells can maintain a low overpotential over 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm−2, and full cells with LiFePO4 cathode can run stably for 1000 cycles at 10 C. This work provides a new path for designing high‐performance PVDF‐based SPEs.

title: Multilayer 3D/2D Perovskite Heterojunctions: Structural Engineering, Interfacial Modulation, and Photovoltaic Applications
content:
This review examines how interface location, phase composition, and crystal orientation govern the performance of multilayer 3D/2D perovskite heterojunctions. It connects structural design with defect passivation, selective charge transport, and suppressed ion migration, highlighting strategies for improving solar cell efficiency and stability and advancing applications in large‐area modules, tandem solar cells, and flexible devices.








ABSTRACT
Perovskite solar cells combine excellent optoelectronic properties with solution processability, but their long‐term performance remains limited by interfacial defects, ion migration and structural instability. Multilayer 3D/2D perovskite heterojunctions offer a promising route to address these limitations by integrating efficient light absorption and charge transport of three‐dimensional perovskites with defect passivation effect and high stability of two‐dimensional perovskites. However, poorly controlled formation of low‐dimensional phases usually introduce mixed dimensionalities, unfavorable orientations, excessive organic spacers and energetic barriers, thereby compromising charge extraction and long‐term stability. Here, we review the evolution of multilayer 3D/2D heterojunctions in terms of interface location, phase composition and crystallographic orientation, and compare solution, thermal evaporation, imprint‐transfer and vapor‐assisted fabrication strategies. We further discuss their roles in defect passivation, energy‐level regulation, charge transport, phase‐structure control and phase stabilization, and highlight their emerging applications in large‐area modules, tandem and flexible devices. Finally, we outline key opportunities in deterministic phase control, interface‐specific asymmetric design, operando characterization, and scalable fabrication to advance multilayer 3D/2D heterojunctions from empirical interface modification toward rationally engineered and manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Depth‐Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB‐SEM Tomography
content:
In FIB–SEM tomography of highly porous polymeric electrodes, subsurface fibers visible through open pores are mistaken for in‐plane material, distorting 3D reconstructions. A machine‐learning‐based depth‐aware model trained on everyday photographs, combined with unsupervised clustering, isolates the exposed fiber cross‐sections without labeled data, agreeing more closely with experimental benchmarks.








ABSTRACT
Quantitative three‐dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub‐micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily reconstruct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out‐of‐plane material as in‐plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interface area. Here, we introduce an annotation‐free, depth‐aware machine‐learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on macroscale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate in‐plane polymer cross‐sections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB–SEM tomography images. Applied to copper‐coated electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quantitative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high‐resolution wide‐angle X‐ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore cross‐section diameter, fiber volume ratio, and Cu depth decrease metrics. This work establishes depth‐aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real‐scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labeled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure–property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.
